content.text:
I submitted index 7 (Mg 0.57 / Mn 0.43) as the best composition, but its photocurrent is only 2e-8 A. That signal is tiny, so this probably isn't a strong photoanode, and I can't tell how close it is to the best composition in the library.

All 3 merit measurements are used. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so none of the phase assignments below were checked against the films.

| Index | Mg fraction | Photocurrent (A) | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.32 | 0 | Closest to MgMn₂O₄ spinel: stable in the MACE model, predicted gap 2.87 eV (below the 3.22 eV light) |
| 7 | 0.57 | 2e-8 | Near Mg₇Mn₅O₁₂, predicted gap 2.71 eV |
| 24 | 0.71 | -1e-8 | Near Mg₈Mn₃O₁₁, predicted gap 3.32 eV, just above the photon energy |

- **Spinel result:** the spinel was my strongest prediction and gave nothing. The stability and band-gap models didn't predict which composition would actually produce photocurrent.
- **Not measured:**
  - **Mn-rich end (Mg below 0.2):** skipped because the phases predicted there have narrow gaps of about 0.9–1.4 eV and seemed unlikely photoanodes. That was a judgement, not a measurement.
  - **Most Mg-rich end (Mg above 0.76):** also untested.
